items.title: Try a 10 to 20 minute walk after dinner
items.text: Walking after a meal is linked to a smaller rise in sugar, with the biggest difference seen after dinner. Walking for 10 to 19 minutes seems to get most of the gain, with a rise about 17.5 mg/dL smaller.

items.title: Move dinner earlier
items.text: Having dinner at 8 pm or later is linked to a rise in sugar, with dinners from 8-9 pm linked to a rise about 13.3 mg/dL more than dinners before 6 pm. Try to start dinner before 8 pm to see if it makes a difference for you.

items.title: Aim for a 13-hour overnight break
items.text: Your overnight fast averaged 10.3 hours, and it's worth trying to extend it to see if it makes a difference for you. In one program, adding an overnight fast to coaching changed some numbers, but it's not clear if it will work for you.
